name: Schengen short-stay visa (Type C) / visa-free entry

requirements.blocker_text: Covers tourism, business visits, and family visits; does not authorise employment or self-employment.
requirements.fix_path: Apply for the relevant work or self-employment route instead if the purpose is employment.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires sufficient funds for the intended stay and travel medical insurance covering at least EUR 30,000, valid across the Schengen area.
requirements.fix_path: Provide bank statements and qualifying travel medical insurance.

evidence_required.document: Passport valid at least 3 months beyond intended departure
Travel medical insurance, minimum EUR 30,000 coverage
Proof of accommodation, itinerary, and sufficient funds

outcome.duration_length: up to 90 days in any 180-day period
outcome.physical_presence_requirement: max 90 days per 180-day rolling window across the whole Schengen area, not just Italy

sources.title: Ministero degli Affari Esteri e della Cooperazione Internazionale (esteri.it) -- Visto per l'Italia, official visa portal

notes: Italy follows the standard EU Schengen Borders Code framework for short-stay entry, identical in structure to Poland's equivalent route elsewhere in this dataset -- both are full Schengen members, so the 90/180 rule, funds/insurance tests, and no-work restriction are common EU law rather than Italy-specific policy. Change of status to a long-term category from inside Italy while on this status is not permitted; applicants must apply for the target visa from outside Italy.
